payload.partitioning:
RELATION MEANING for this matrix, one only: "must happen before, and its failure invalidates the later one" - a strict ordering-and-dependency relation. Chosen because every coupling here is temporal-with-consequence; mixing in data coupling would make the clusters meaningless.

COUPLING REASONS, classified:
- Sequence with consequence: F3 (name the record) must precede F5/F6 (combine, withhold), because withholding before naming is how content becomes unfindable. F2 (detect emptiness) must precede everything, because there is nothing to name or merge otherwise.
- Shared failure mode: F5, F6 and F9 (refuse on doubt) share one - a partial application. Any of them failing must leave trunk untouched, so they belong in one atomic unit.
- Same lifecycle: F1 (capture progress) fires repeatedly during the iteration; every other close-side function fires exactly once, at the end. Different lifecycle, so different cluster.
- Same external interface: F11 (equip a working place) and F12 (warn on divergence) both act at open, against git and the toolchain.
- Independent: F10 (keep ended work visible) reads the grant index and touches neither git's tree nor the merge.

CLUSTERS (four, plus one standing constraint):
- CLUSTER A - THE MILESTONE LANE: F1. Fires per bless, on the branch only. Basic function.
- CLUSTER B - THE CLOSE, ATOMIC: F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F9. One unit because of the shared failure mode; ordered inside as F2 -> F3 -> F4 -> F5 -> F6, with F9 wrapping all of it and F7 as the property the unit must preserve. Basic function, and the safety-critical one.
- CLUSTER C - THE POINTER: F8. Fires per bless (it writes the tag onto the grant), so it shares CLUSTER A's lifecycle, but it serves the auditor rather than durability. Support function, deliberately not folded into A - one writes a commit, the other writes a record field.
- CLUSTER D - THE WORKING PLACE: F11, F12. Fires at open, against the toolchain and git. Support function.
- STANDING: F13 (protect the record from erasure) is not a cluster - it is a constraint over every other function, enforced wherever git is invoked. Safety function.

The tear is between A/C (per-bless, cheap, repeated) and B (once, atomic, safety-critical): they share no failure mode, and B's refusal must never be able to undo A's committed milestones.
